MarcusKvCtx.physicalReading: A two-level ladder (radiative rad, nonradiative ic) whose S₂→S₁ internal conversion is the Marcus-form activated step at reorganization energy lam and gap x, compared at tolerance tol. The Marcus barrier sets the squared-gap window; the ladder decides whether the upper block emits.

EglRateCtx.physicalReading: One nonradiative step in the equal-curvature two-parabola model: pre-exponential A, reorganization energy lam, thermal energy kB*T and driving force x. Both theories evaluate their own rate law on this same parameter tuple.

EglZoneCtx.physicalReading: The reorganization energy and driving force of one step. The two theories classify this point into the same region: the gap larger than the reorganization energy.

MarcusICCtx.physicalReading: One internal-conversion step: pre-exponential A, channel reorganization energy lam, thermal energy kB*T and the channel gap x. ICvsISC evaluates its IC rate law on this tuple; Marcus evaluates its activated rate on the same tuple.

MarcusSSCtx.physicalReading: The displaced-parabola pair of the same fluorophore: reorganization energy lam and 0-0 energy e00. Marcus classifies (lam, e00); StokesShift computes the vertical absorption and emission energies from the same pair.

KashaVavCtx.physicalReading: The Kasha ladder up to excitation level N: radiative and nonradiative rate arrays and the level N at which the excitation enters. Kasha states the exact rule as upperYield = 0; KashaVavilov states the spectral invariance of the same ladder.

KashaEglCtx.physicalReading: One internal-conversion step in the Marcus form: pre-exponential A, reorganization energy lam, thermal energy kB*T and gap x. The Kasha ladder fills its inter-level IC channel with this rate; the energy-gap law writes its nonradiative rate on the same tuple.

KashaEinsteinCtx.physicalReading: One excited state with radiative rate A and total nonradiative loss kNR. The Kasha ladder resolves it into a radiative and a nonradiative branch; the Einstein side writes the same radiative fraction as A times the observed lifetime 1/(A+kNR).

KvQyCtx.physicalReading: The Kasha ladder up to level N. The KashaVavilov total-yield row splits the fluorescence yield into the lowest-level emission and the upper-block leak; the QuantumYield calculus evaluates the lowest-level two-channel yield.

KvFpCtx.physicalReading: The S₁ state with fluorescence, intersystem-crossing and internal-conversion rates. FluorPhos keeps the three channels separate; the Kasha ladder resolves the same state into one radiative and one nonradiative channel, the latter carrying kISC + kIC.

KvSvCtx.physicalReading: The Kasha ladder up to level N under a collisional quencher at concentration q with bimolecular rate kq. Dynamic quenching adds kq*q to the *level-0* total decay; the upper levels of the ladder are untouched.

MarcusForsterDisjointCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context only: the Marcus step carries an activation barrier with a driving-force coordinate, the Förster transfer carries a donor lifetime and a donor-acceptor separation with an R⁻⁶ rate law. No declared translation relates a separation to a driving force.

MarcusEinsteinDisjointCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context only: the Marcus rate is an activated nonradiative step; the Einstein coefficients are radiative transition quantities with a radiation-density factor. The single symbol A means a pre-exponential on one side and a spontaneous-emission coefficient on the other; no translation is declared.

KashaStokesDisjointCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context only: the ladder carries rate arrays and yields; the Stokes description carries the two parabola offsets (lam, e00) and no rate array. No declared translation turns a rate array into a band position.

KashaICCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the ladder channelling S₂→S₁ conversion through the ICvsISC Arrhenius rate law at that step’s own reorganization energy and gap. The ladder leaves ic a free rate array, so the assignment ic 1 = icRate is a modelling premise that no delivered statement carries.

KashaForsterDisjointCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context only: the ladder emits and converts between its own levels; the Förster description transfers excitation between two chromophores through a dipole geometry. No donor-acceptor pair and no donor lifetime occur in the ladder.

KvEglCandidateCtx.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the energy-gap law’s nonradiative rate fills the ladder’s IC channel, which would decide whether the Vavilov invariance survives. The ladder carries no energy-gap parameter of its own, and the delivered window row is stated with the Kasha-side Marcus-form rate, not with the energy-gap-law rate.

queries.title: A gap outside the Marcus window makes anti-Kasha emission observable
queries.chemicalQuestion: If the ladder’s S₂→S₁ internal conversion obeys the Marcus rate at reorganization energy lam and gap x, does a squared gap outside the Kasha tolerance window force a positive emission yield from the upper block — i.e. an observable failure of the Kasha rule rather than Vavilov spectral invariance?
queries.chemicalRationale: Marcus supplies the energy-gap control of an internal-conversion step: the barrier (lam − x)²/(4·lam) is smallest at x = lam, so the conversion rate is maximal there and falls quadratically as the gap leaves the reorganization energy. The KashaVavilov layer decides whether the ladder keeps the lowest-state spectrum (SpecSame, the Vavilov side) or leaks emission from above (anti-Kasha observable). The query composes the two statements: once the Marcus-controlled squared gap exceeds the Kasha window bound, the upper block necessarily retains emission. It is a cross-theory implication whose antecedent is a Marcus barrier condition and whose consequent is the KashaVavilov anti-Kasha predicate, not an identity of two rate notations.

sharedContext.physicalReading: A two-level ladder (radiative rad, nonradiative ic) whose S₂→S₁ internal conversion is the Marcus-form activated step at reorganization energy lam and gap x, compared at tolerance tol. The Marcus barrier sets the squared-gap window; the ladder decides whether the upper block emits.

left.requirement: The Marcus barrier is evaluated at the shared (lam, x); the prefactor, thermal energy and tolerance are carried only as premise parameters.

queries.title: The energy-gap-law nonradiative rate is the Marcus rate
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the energy-gap law’s nonradiative rate — the Arrhenius rate over the equal-curvature crossing barrier — literally the Marcus rate at the same pre-exponential factor, reorganization energy, thermal energy and driving force?
queries.chemicalRationale: The energy-gap law and the Marcus inverted region describe the same nonradiative step: an activated crossing of the two equal-curvature parabolas, with the gap as the driving force. The energy-gap-law module keeps its own copy of the barrier and rate for independence, and its delivered certificate pins that copy to the Marcus body. The query asks whether the two theories’ nonradiative rate is one and the same rate law, so that the gap-law’s gap dependence is the Marcus barrier’s quadratic dependence. The answer is yes, definitionally.

queries.title: The energy-gap-law inverted gap is the Marcus inverted region
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the gap region in which the energy-gap law’s rate decreases with driving force — the inverted gap — exactly the Marcus inverted region?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both predicates cut the (lam, x) plane at x = lam: above it the barrier grows with the gap, so the rate falls. The two theories state the same boundary for the same physical reason (the parabola crossing moves past the reactant minimum), and the energy-gap-law certificate pins its predicate to the Marcus one. The query asks for the region-level identity that the rate-level identity of the companion query presupposes.

queries.title: The emission window is open exactly in the Marcus inverted region
queries.chemicalQuestion: Does the Stokes emission energy become positive (`0 < emEnergy`) — a vertical photon above the 0-0 energy — exactly in the Marcus inverted region (`InvertedRegion`, lam < e00), and is it negative or zero outside that region (normal region e00 < lam, and the zero-photon corner e00 = lam)?
queries.chemicalRationale: The Stokes module computes the vertical absorption and emission energies from the same displaced-parabola pair that Marcus classifies. Its emission energy is e00 − lam, which changes sign at e00 = lam — exactly the Marcus region boundary. The delivered row SS-C9 records the sign identity against `Marcus.InvertedRegion`. The query asks whether the optical emission-window sign is the Marcus region predicate, which is the one genuine Marcus/StokesShift statement-level contact (the surfaces are only kernel copies).

queries.title: Is the Förster transfer rate an activated Marcus step?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the Förster resonance transfer rate — a through-space dipolar process with an R⁻⁶ distance law and a donor lifetime — the Marcus activated rate at the same driving force?
queries.chemicalRationale: Förster transfer is not an activated crossing: its rate is set by the spectral overlap and the donor–acceptor separation, and its only energy is the donor transition energy. Marcus’s rate is an activated barrier over a reaction coordinate with a reorganization energy and a driving force. The two models share no scalar: a translation from (tauD, r6, R) to (lam, x) is not a coordinate change of either declared model. The question is outside the declared jurisdiction, not logically false — and an Arrhenius shape alone must not be read as identifying a barrier with a transfer geometry.

sharedContext.physicalReading: Candidate shared context only: the Marcus step carries an activation barrier with a driving-force coordinate, the Förster transfer carries a donor lifetime and a donor-acceptor separation with an R⁻⁶ rate law. No declared translation relates a separation to a driving force.

queries.title: Is the Marcus rate an Einstein spontaneous-emission coefficient?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the Marcus activation-controlled rate the Einstein A coefficient of the same transition — i.e. is the nonradiative activated step the radiative spontaneous-emission process?
queries.chemicalRationale: The Einstein coefficients describe radiative transitions: A₂₁ is fixed by the radiation-density factor and the B coefficient, and the radiative lifetime is 1/A. The Marcus rate is an activated nonradiative step whose scale is set by a barrier and a pre-exponential factor. The symbol A means a pre-exponential on one side and a spontaneous-emission coefficient on the other — a notation collision, not a shared object. The two models have no shared scalar; the only machine contact of the Einstein side runs through the QuantumYield calculus, which is a different pair.

The delivered pieces are the gap-law rate identity to Marcus (in the EnergyGapLaw module), the Kasha window row (stated with the Kasha-side `marcusIC` object), and the D2 anti-Kasha boundary. What is missing is a delivered statement that carries the gap-law rate into the ladder and out to the Vavilov predicate; the delivered EnergyGapLaw§16 registration lists KashaVavilov as an undelivered composition candidate. The query is therefore unresolved with the gap recorded precisely.

sharedContext.physicalReading: Candidate shared context: the energy-gap law’s nonradiative rate fills the ladder’s IC channel, which would decide whether the Vavilov invariance survives. The ladder carries no energy-gap parameter of its own, and the delivered window row is stated with the Kasha-side Marcus-form rate, not with the energy-gap-law rate.

right.requirement: The translation is a candidate, which is why the query is unresolved rather than certified.

nonClaims: Sixteen pairs, seventeen queries: one query per pair except P-Marcus-EnergyGapLaw, which carries two chemically distinct statement-level queries.
Screened is not the same as certified; the package records pair coverage separately from outcome counts.
One query per pair does not exhaust all conceivable relations between the theories outside the frozen bounded query protocol.
The certified rows are probe-level Lean certificates over delivered statements; they are not claims that the delivered theories are complete models of the chemistry.
The outOfScope rows are jurisdiction records about statement-level vocabulary; they do not claim that the physical processes are unrelated.
No R5 acceptance is claimed: the package stays submitted until independent review.
